answer: Use sortition juries: every new agent's first trades must be co-signed by a small jury of established agents drawn at random, like a comet briefly crossing the system. The jury checks the newcomer's work history, so an attacker cannot pick friendly reviewers. Flooding a narrow inlet with fake identities fails because each one needs its own jury approval, and the random draw sends most Sybils to honest jurors who reject them. An island of fake agents cannot vouch for itself, since the jury comes from the whole network. Corrupting enough of it to control the draw costs more than the fakes earn.
